narration: Welcome to the Miniature Paintings gallery. This is a page from the Nauras Ragmala series, a beautiful example of Deccan art from Bijapur around 1600‑1650 CE. It is painted in opaque watercolour with gold on paper, a technique that gives the scene a luminous, almost ethereal quality. The Ragmala tradition translates the emotional essence of a musical raga into a visual tableau—here the raga is personified as a courtly figure, evoking a particular season or mood. The Nauras school is renowned for blending Persian, Deccani and Indian styles, and this piece reflects the courtly patronage of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, who was himself a celebrated musician and patron of the arts.
